response.sql:
WITH qualifying_patients AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ID
  FROM Laboratory
  WHERE `U-PRO` = '-' AND RA = '-'
), per_patient AS (
  SELECT l.ID,
         AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt,
         AVG(l.TAT - l.TAT2) AS avg_tat_difference
  FROM Laboratory AS l
  JOIN qualifying_patients AS q ON q.ID = l.ID
  GROUP BY l.ID
)
SELECT AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_of_patient_pt_averages,
       AVG(avg_tat_difference) AS avg_of_patient_tat_difference_averages
FROM per_patient;

assumptions.assumption: A patient qualifies if any single laboratory record has both U-PRO and RA exactly '-'; the per-patient averages then use all of that patient's laboratory records. SQL AVG ignores null values, including when either TAT or TAT2 is missing for a record.
